Classify each system as AI, machine learning, both, or neither based on the lecture: (a) an expert system that follows specialists' IF/THEN rules; (b) a model that learns churn patterns from historical data; (c) a deep neural network trained on examples. Explain the nesting relationships among AI, ML, neural networks, and deep learning.

The lecture contrasts statistics as more model-driven and data science as more data-driven. Explain these two starting points using one question about explaining an association and one question about predicting future behavior. Then discuss why the contrast should not be treated as a strict boundary between the fields.

A university plans to use past admissions decisions to predict which applicants will succeed. Identify how this could be a data science and machine-learning project, describe the role of domain expertise, and analyze two ethical risks the university should address before acting on predictions.
